html:
SMTO-EXE-0246 — Docker reported a problem with this action

GUID: 538c2cd4-80ed-51eb-a779-26a3f810a4b1
Slug: docker-operation-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • Docker tried the action on the Gateway computer but reported that it failed, without saying exactly why. Depending on when it failed, part of the action may already have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In this conversation, ask SMTO to show the logs for the container or Compose project involved. The error alone does not establish the cause, but Docker's own logs usually name it, such as a port already in use or a missing file.
  2. Ask SMTO to show the current state of the containers, images or project, without changing anything. This shows whether part of the action already happened before it failed.
  3. Fix the cause the logs point to, for example stop whatever is using the same port or correct the Compose file, then ask SMTO to do whatever is still missing. Trying again only helps once the reason for the failure is gone.

What success looks like

  • The action completes and SMTO reports success, and the container or project is running as expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the logs SMTO showed you, to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't keep repeating the same action without checking what already changed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Docker Engine returned an unclassified error status or stream error, or a Compose command exited unsuccessfully, without a narrower cause; this does not always prove the request was rejected before it took effect.

What this means

  • The Engine returned an unclassified error status/stream error, Compose exited unsuccessfully or a service exception lacked a narrower category. This does not always prove pre-dispatch rejection. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The Engine returned an unclassified error status/stream error, Compose exited unsuccessfully or a service exception lacked a narrower category. This does not always prove pre-dispatch rejection.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect endpoint/operation, bounded progress and effect flags; avoid treating every generic failure as an invalid argument.

How to fix it

  • Read the receipt and the Engine or Compose logs on the Gateway host (docker.container_logs, docker.compose_logs, or journalctl -u docker). Inspect current state read-only, correct the demonstrated cause (port conflict, bad image, invalid Compose service, container state), then issue a new request.
  • Inspect the retained failure and reconcile possible effects; correct the specific cause when supported by evidence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The original outcome is understood and its actual cause is corrected before new work.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
